name: United States Senate Youth Program (USSYP)
value: $12,500 undergraduate scholarship for each delegate, plus program-paid travel, lodging and meals for Washington Week, March 6 to March 13, 2027. Parents pay transport to and from the departure airport or station.
deadline: Student application deadlines vary by state and are earlier than the December 1, 2026 state delegate-certification deadline. Arizona lists September 10, 2026. Mandatory Washington Week: March 6 to March 13, 2027.
apply: Obtain the application from your state selection contact or school principal, counselor or social-studies teacher. State education officials select two delegates and two alternates. Selected students and parents sign participation and conduct agreements; attendance for the entire Washington Week is required to receive the scholarship.
eligibility: U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents who are high-school juniors or seniors throughout 2026-27, living and attending school in the state they represent with a parent or guardian resident there. An eligible elected or appointed leadership role must be held throughout the school year and represent or serve a constituency. Home-school applicants require state education approval; specified military and interstate-school exceptions apply. Previous delegates/scholarship recipients and fall 2026 graduates are ineligible.
notes: Qualifying roles include student-government/class officers, student council representatives, honor-society officers and approved year-round civic/educational representatives. Ordinary academic-club, debate, Model UN, sports, conference and self-created-group leadership do not qualify. Do not use the national December 1 certification date as your student application deadline.

name: National High School Oratorical Contest
value: National winner $25,000; second $22,500; third $20,000; each state winner in the national first round $2,000, plus $2,000 more for advancing past round one. Over $203,500 total.
deadline: Local post and state department entry dates vary. The 2027 national finals are May 14 to May 16, 2027 at Hillsdale College, Michigan, with mandatory orientation on Friday evening.
apply: Contact your local American Legion post or state department. Advance through local and state contests; each department certifies one national contestant. Deliver an 8-to-10-minute Constitutional oration and a 3-to-5-minute assigned-topic speech without notes, props or amplification. The four 2027 assigned topics are posted. Both speeches are required for scholarship payment.
eligibility: U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents under 20 on the national contest date, enrolled in grades 9-12 at high-school level, including home school. Enter only one department in which you reside or attend school. Early graduates may compete if not enrolled in higher education at the state finals. Previous national top-three finalists cannot compete again.
notes: Awards may be used at a U.S. college or university. National contestant and chaperone travel/lodging are paid; the chaperone must be over 21.

provider: National Society Daughters of the American Revolution
name: DAR Good Citizens Award and Scholarship Contest
value: Scholarships for essay winners at the chapter, state, division and national levels (amounts not stated on the official page)
deadline: Not stated on the official page; set by local DAR chapters
apply: Your school selects one senior as its DAR Good Citizen; that student may then enter the scholarship contest with a personal statement and an essay. Ask your school counselor or a local DAR chapter.
eligibility: One high-school senior per participating accredited school, selected by teachers and peers for dependability, service, leadership and patriotism. The school must be accredited and in good standing with its state board; the official handout also describes recognized accreditation allowing a diploma without a GED. U.S. citizenship is not required.
notes: This school-selected contest uses local DAR chapter instructions. The general DAR Scholarship Committee online portal is not the entry route for Good Citizens.

name: Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision
value: First prize (4 teams): per student, a $10,000 Series EE savings bond at maturity, $5,000 cash, or $5,000 to a 529 plan. Second prize (4 teams): $5,000 bond, $2,500 cash, or $2,500 to a 529 plan. Finalists get a Washington, DC trip.
deadline: Coach submits the project online by 8:00 PM ET, January 27, 2027
apply: Form a team of two to four students with a coach age 21 or older, who registers and submits online. Include a title (50 characters maximum), abstract (150 words maximum), description (11 pages maximum), bibliography and one-page Technology Launch Flyer. High-school descriptions cover present technology, history, future technology at least 10 years ahead, breakthroughs, three rejected alternatives and consequences. Regional winners subsequently build a prototype.
eligibility: U.S. or Canadian citizens living in the U.S., Canada, U.S. territories or a DoWEA school abroad, enrolled full time and no older than 21. The oldest team member sets the category; high-school category is grades 10-12. One project per student. NSTA employees, board members, judges and their families are excluded. Previous regional/national finalists need a new team of previously nonfinalist students; previously prize-winning projects are ineligible.
notes: AI may support brainstorming or research under the official policy; cite original sources and link the full LLM-generated text. The flyer prototype image must not be AI-generated. Savings-bond figures are maturity values, with issue price half the face value; Canadian winners receive equivalent cash.

name: U.S. Stockholm Junior Water Prize
value: Published U.S. national award: $10,000 per winning project and a paid trip to Stockholm. WEF lists a $15,000 international award plus $5,000 for the winner's school, expressly subject to change. The 2027 international prize terms are unconfirmed.
deadline: 2027 competition dates are not published. The latest official eligibility page still lists April 15, 2026 for state entry, virtual national judging in May 2026 and in-person finals June 8 to June 10, 2026.
apply: Under the latest published rules, submit the state online form and a research paper (maximum 2 MB); one team member submits information for both. Regional science-fair recognition is optional and self-nomination is allowed. State winners submit a national paper following national guidelines, attend virtual judging and, if selected in the top 20, in-person finals. The national winning project must send at least one member to Stockholm or the prize passes to the runner-up. Current 2027 application stages and portal are unconfirmed.
eligibility: The latest rules allow grade 9-12 students who conduct water-related scientific research and reach age 15 by August 1 of the competition year. Individuals and two-person teams may enter; state competition is limited to residents of the 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico. Current 2027 rules are not yet published.
notes: The U.S. award is per project. National finalists must be available for required judging, and the U.S. winning project must be represented at the international competition.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) Grand Awards
value: Category Grand Awards: $6,000, $2,400, $1,200 and $600 cash. Top awards selected from first-place projects include $100,000, two $75,000 awards and two $50,000 awards. Team awards are split equally. Some top awards are restricted to post-secondary educational expenses.
deadline: Qualify through an affiliated fair with its own entry dates; the latest permitted 2027 affiliated-fair date is April 12, 2027. Finalist questionnaire and official party registration are due within 12 calendar days of the fair; virtual booth within 12 days of booth assignment. Abstract rewrites only are due April 16, 2027. ISEF: May 8 to May 14, 2027 in Los Angeles.
apply: Compete at a Society-affiliated fair and earn a finalist allocation. Before research, complete the research plan and required sponsor, student and approval forms; obtain any required SRC/IRB approval before experimentation. Finalists submit scanned paperwork, a maximum 250-word abstract, registration and virtual booth, and present the project at ISEF.
eligibility: Grade 9-12 students or equivalent, selected by an affiliated fair, who have not reached age 20 on or before May 1 preceding ISEF. Individual or maximum three-member team projects; one project per student. Research is limited to 12 continuous months, starting no earlier than January 2026 and ending by May 2027. International students are eligible.
notes: Affiliated fairs may impose additional geographic and entry restrictions. Continuations must demonstrate substantive new research and undergo annual review. Generative AI cannot write the research plan, abstract or poster or create citations; permitted resource use must be acknowledged. Team membership cannot change after a project competes at any fair.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
value: 2026 prize: $250,000 undergraduate scholarship, $50,000 for an eligible inspiring teacher and up to $100,000 for school science-lab work. The scholarship is paid directly to an accredited institution for approved education costs and must be used within eight years of high-school graduation.
deadline: 2026 video/application entry closed September 15, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. PDT. Existing entrants must finish at least five peer reviews by September 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. PDT. The 2027 entry cycle is not published.
apply: The 2026 process required an individual original English-language science or mathematics video of at most two minutes on YouTube, not private, plus an application and at least five peer reviews. Evaluation-panel review, popular vote and final judging follow. Current 2027 instructions are unconfirmed.
eligibility: 2026 entrants had to be at least 13 by May 11, 2026 and not yet 19 on October 1, 2026. Minors needed parent/guardian permission. Group entries, prior sponsor-competition winners, sponsor-connected persons and residents or persons barred under the stated sanctions restrictions were excluded. Current 2027 age dates and other rules are unconfirmed.
notes: One entry per person. Popular vote can advance one entry; judges choose the final winner. The teacher and lab awards do not go to the student. Current 2027 prize terms and eligibility must be checked when published.

name: Diamond Challenge
value: Each track: first place $12,000, second $8,000, third $4,500 per team, plus topical prizes.
deadline: Submission by January 14, 2027 at 5 p.m. EST. Advancing teams notified February 10, 2027; finalists announced March 9, 2027. Mandatory in-person final round at the Limitless World Summit, April 29 to April 30, 2027.
apply: Choose business or social innovation and either live or virtual pitching when applying. Submit a three-to-five-page English PDF narrative, double spaced, 12-point font with one-inch margins, and a public 60-second introduction video. Advancing teams deliver a five-minute live or recorded pitch with a deck; live pitches have three-minute questions. Finalists submit a public Google Slides deck and pitch in person.
eligibility: Worldwide teams of two to four high-school students ages 14-18 at the submission deadline, with one registered advisor age 21 or older. Each student joins only one team and enters one concept. Ventures must not have generated more than $100,000 revenue before the deadline; previous Summit-finalist concepts cannot be resubmitted.
notes: At least one team member must attend the Summit. Teams unable to attend because of denied or delayed visas may request a one-year deferral. Awards are paid to a registered venture or split equally among registered members; absent agreement, they are split equally. Previously participating nonteam concept creators must be disclosed. $100,000 is the combined prize pool, not the amount awarded to one team.

name: The Paradigm Challenge
value: For teams of four or more: grand prize $100,000 instead of first place $10,000; other age-division first places $10,000, seconds $2,000, thirds $1,000; other finalists up to $200 per team. For teams smaller than four, each qualifying member receives 25% of the listed team prize ($25,000 for the grand prize; $50 for other finalists).
deadline: May 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. PST, as stated in the official rules. Finalists announced by June 1, 2027.
apply: Register and submit an English-language entry online, individually or in a team of any size. Provide team and member details, an idea statement of at most 140 characters, idea category and explanation, and participation-question responses. Files or video links are optional. Multiple entries and teams are allowed; new entries are required even for previous entrants.
eligibility: Ages 4 to 18 on submission, with parent or legal-guardian permission. International participants are eligible except residents of U.S.-sanctioned jurisdictions; sponsor-related personnel and their specified family or household members are excluded. The oldest member determines the age division, and any ineligible member disqualifies the whole team.
notes: Judging considers efficacy, feasibility, originality, presentation and collaboration, including outside collaboration for individual entrants. First-place trips cover up to four members and accompanying parents or guardians. Potential winners must return consent and eligibility documents within 72 hours; taxes and unspecified costs are their responsibility. The rules use PST for the May deadline.

name: Stossel in the Classroom Essay Contest
value: High school division: first $2,500, second $1,000, third $500, five finalists $200, five semifinalists $100, 15 honorable mentions $50
deadline: 11:59 PM ET, March 12, 2027
apply: Submit one original English essay of 500 to 1,000 words answering one of four prompts, directly or through a teacher. Cite sources. The works-cited list can count toward the minimum but does not trigger the maximum-word disqualification. Final judging requires a brief interview during May 16 to 22, 2027.
eligibility: High school division: grades 9 to 12, within the contest's ages 10 to 19 during September 9, 2026 to March 12, 2027; reside in the United States, Canada or at a U.S. military address. One essay per writer. You may also enter the video contest but cannot also enter the 2026-27 AI Challenge. Previous first-place winners can receive prizes again only in a different division or contest type. Contest personnel and immediate family members are excluded.
notes: AI-generated content or plagiarism causes disqualification. Finalists must complete the May 16 to 22, 2027 interview; winners are announced May 31, 2027. Cash-prize recipients pay any applicable taxes. Entry authorizes the sponsor to use the essay, while ownership remains with the writer.

name: National Economics Challenge
value: 2027 prizes are unpublished. The 2026 rules awarded each national-final team member and one coach $1,000 for first place, $500 second, $250 third or $200 fourth; lodging and group meals were covered, but travel was not.
deadline: 2027 state registration, national qualifying and finalist-confirmation dates are unpublished. Contact the state coordinator; the current program page offers registration-update alerts.
apply: Start with a coached local team and the state competition. State winners progress to national qualifying rounds. The 2026 rules used teams of three or four, online semifinal tests, and an in-person critical-thinking presentation and quiz bowl; 2027 detailed rules remain unpublished.
eligibility: High school students. The current page places AP, IB, honors and returning competitors in Adam Smith; David Ricardo is for first-time competitors with no more than one economics course. The 2026 rules also required homeschooled students to enter Adam Smith and teams to share a school or eligible organization; those detailed 2027 rules are not yet confirmed.
notes: The program remains active, but 2027 prize amounts, dates and detailed rules are unpublished. Historical 2026 terms are shown for context and should be checked against the new rules.

name: Maureen O'Donnell Scholarship for Academic Excellence
value: Up to 15 scholarships of $2,000 annually. The Fall 2025 newsletter describes annual renewal while continuing Latin, Greek or Classics; complete 2027 renewal requirements are not published.
deadline: Not stated on the official page; applications are mailed to eligible gold medalists
apply: Earn a gold medal on an Advanced NLE exam; an application is then mailed to you.
eligibility: High school seniors who win a gold medal on the Advanced Latin Prose, Advanced Latin Poetry, or Advanced Latin Reading Comprehension Exam.
notes: Recipients must take at least one Latin or classical Greek language course each semester of their first college year; a classics course in translation does not satisfy this requirement. The scholarship application is mailed to qualifying senior gold medalists. The 2027 application deadline and complete renewal conditions have not been published.

name: National Speech & Debate Tournament scholarships
value: Scholarship amounts vary by National Tournament event or recognition category. Individual 2027 award amounts and conditions are unpublished.
deadline: 2027 National Tournament: June 13 to 18, 2027, Phoenix, Arizona. Qualification, registration and scholarship-specific deadlines for 2027 are not yet published.
apply: Compete through NSDA school and district channels to reach the National Tournament. Scholarship awards differ by competition or recognition category. The latest 2026 instructions require graduated recipients to provide proof of postsecondary enrollment and claim awarded funds through the scholarship-claim form; payments go to the registrar.
eligibility: High school speech and debate competitors. Tournament and scholarship eligibility vary by event and award. The 2026 rules also permitted limited supplemental-event entries by nonqualifiers with school and student NSDA membership; complete 2027 qualification and award restrictions are unpublished.
notes: This is a collection of National Tournament awards, not one uniform scholarship. The 2027 event dates and location are confirmed, but prize breakdowns, qualification deadlines and scholarship rules remain unpublished. The college-scholarship listing form is for colleges to supply listings, not for students to apply. The NSDA directory reports more than $100,000 in scholarships across the tournament, not an individual award.

name: Army ROTC Four-Year Scholarship (High School)
value: Four-year scholarship: full tuition and allowable fees, or a $12,000 annual room-and-board allowance paid $6,000 per semester/$4,000 per quarter instead of tuition and fees; plus $420 per month for ten school-year months and $1,200 annually for books.
deadline: Round 1 due October 12, 2026; Round 2 due January 18, 2027; Round 3 due March 8, 2027. Applications must be started by March 4, 2027.
apply: Create an online Army ROTC scholarship account and complete the application, high-school academic and SAT/ACT information, physical fitness assessment and Professor of Military Science interview. Contact the Recruiting Operations Officer at a participating school. Medical qualification or an approved waiver is required before contracting.
eligibility: High-school applicants normally need 2.5 unweighted GPA, SAT/ACT scores, a high-school diploma or equivalent before September 1 of the award year, Army medical, height/weight and fitness standards, age at least 17 by the first scholarship semester and under 31 during the commissioning calendar year. The current scholarship regulation permits U.S. citizens or U.S. nationals before contracting; dual citizens must be willing to renounce the other citizenship if requested for security clearance. Under-18 contracting requires parental consent. GPA waivers require Cadet Command approval.
notes: Acceptance carries an eight-year Army service obligation; active-duty versus Reserve/National Guard requirements depend on the scholarship and contract. Scholarship recipients may leave before entering sophomore year without obligation. Continued benefits require full-time enrollment, degree progress, at least 2.0 term and cumulative academic and ROTC GPAs, and military fitness/height/weight and conduct standards. The room-and-board election excludes fees.

name: AFROTC High School Scholarship Program
value: Four-year scholarships: Type 1 uncapped tuition, Type 2 up to $18,000 per year or Type 4 up to $36,000 per year; plus $900 annually for books and a monthly stipend after contracting. Annual housing conversion can cover university-contracted housing up to $10,000 instead of tuition; request before the fall term each year.
deadline: For 2027-28: Board 1 initial application September 15, 2026; documents/eligibility September 25, 2026; interview October 16, 2026; acceptance March 1, 2027. Board 2 initial application December 11, 2026; documents/test scores December 22, 2026 (11:59 p.m. CST); interview March 5, 2027; acceptance May 31, 2027.
apply: Use WINGS to complete the eligibility questionnaire, school/major preferences, counselor form, grades 9 to 11 transcript, official SAT/ACT/CLT scores directly from the testing agency, activity and youth-experience information, acknowledgments and civil/military disclosures. Complete the current fitness form and the assigned officer interview after eligibility review. Recommendation letters are not accepted. Medical clearance begins after a scholarship offer.
eligibility: Entering college and AFROTC in 2027-28, with no prior full-time postsecondary enrollment except qualifying high-school dual enrollment. At least 3.3 unweighted cumulative GPA through the last complete school year, SAT 1310/ACT 28/CLT 93 from one test without superscoring; ACT Science is mandatory. At least 17 at activation and at most 30 by December 31 of commissioning year. Citizenship must be obtained by the end of the first freshman term and before activation. Homeschooled students are eligible; prior-service applicants have additional release/separation requirements.
notes: The 2027-28 application fitness assessment is one timed 2-mile run, one minute of pushups and one minute of situps, administered by an authorized school official or guardian; only one score sheet is allowed. Temporary medical exemptions require documentation. Activation requires contracting and medical clearance, and awards must be used in the awarded degree category. Sophomore continuation is competitive. The standard nonrated Air Force commitment is four active-duty years; aviation roles have longer training-related obligations. Recipients can withdraw before sophomore year without scholarship repayment or service obligation. Exact scholarship GPA retention conditions should be confirmed with the detachment.

name: NROTC Four-Year National Scholarship
value: Four-year full tuition and selected educational fees, or room and board up to $11,500 annually; $750 per academic year for textbooks, uniforms/Naval Science textbooks, three summer cruises and monthly academic-year subsistence: $250 freshman, $300 sophomore, $350 junior and $400 senior. Complete ongoing scholarship retention terms require confirmation.
deadline: Fiscal year 2027 Navy, Nurse and Marine option online applications close at midnight January 31, 2027; the official portal does not state the time zone. Coordinate completion of supporting materials with the recruiter.
apply: Create a Netfocus application account and review the official application-information checklist with a Navy or Marine recruiter. The available checklist calls for signed understanding, debarment and drug statements, officer interview(s), teacher recommendations, transcripts and official test scores. Navy/Nurse applicants take the Applicant Fitness Assessment; Marine applicants take the Marine fitness test. Confirm the final 2027 package with the recruiter.
eligibility: High-school graduates admitted to an approved NROTC college, at least 17 and not yet 23 by September 1 of the college-start year; U.S. citizens or applicants in the naturalization process. Navy medical/fitness, criminal-record and test requirements apply and vary by option. Complete current requirements and precise option-specific score thresholds could not be confirmed from the blocked central requirements page.
notes: Navy Option requires at least five years of active military service; Navy Nurse and Marine options require at least four. Specialty training can entail additional obligations. The FY2027 portal is open and confirms the deadline, but the deadline time zone and complete current eligibility, package and retention rules remain unresolved.

name: Equitable Excellence Scholarship
value: Tentative fall 2027 terms: up to 100 awards of $5,000 per year, renewable for up to three additional years or until a bachelor's degree, whichever occurs first; up to $20,000 total.
deadline: Applications are currently closed. The administrator has not published the next opening or closing date; use its notification sign-up.
apply: Tentative fall 2027 application: online personal statement about paying it forward through college, current complete transcript and the first two pages of the most recent IRS Form 1040, with sensitive identifiers redacted. Submit all materials electronically.
eligibility: Tentative fall 2027 terms require current public high school seniors in the 50 states, District of Columbia or Puerto Rico, financial need, 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale, planned full-time enrollment at an accredited two- or four-year U.S. college, community commitment and a publicity release. Private and home schools are excluded in these tentative terms. Sponsor/administrator employees and specified associates, professionals and immediate family members are excluded.
notes: The official administrator labels all upcoming-program information tentative and subject to change. Published renewal terms require satisfactory academic performance and continued enrollment; recipients must attend one professional-development workshop per college year. A selected teacher receives a separate $500 gift card. Confirm final eligibility when the application opens.

name: National Beta Scholarship
value: Individual awards: $1,000 for 249 recipients, $2,500 for six, and one each of $6,000, $8,000, $10,000, $15,000 and $20,000.
deadline: Opens November 2, 2026; initial application January 14, 2027, 11:59 p.m. EST. Semifinalists announced February 11, 2027; their additional materials due March 14, 2027; winners announced May 1, 2027.
apply: Use your National Beta membership ID and last name to enter the online application. Phase 1 includes unweighted GPA, ACT/SAT scores with an uploaded copy, official or unofficial transcript, Beta events, leadership/awards, service projects/hours and a resume of outside activities, service and honors. The top 100 semifinalists submit one sponsor recommendation, one to three candidate evaluations and two essays.
eligibility: Active 12th-grade Senior Beta members.
notes: Active 12th-grade Senior Beta membership is required. The current page confirms 260 awards and both application phases, but does not explain payment timing or whether any award can be renewed. The application portal is closed until the published opening date. The combined annual scholarship budget exceeds $300,000 across 260 recipients, not one award.

name: Bennington Young Writers Awards
value: Cash by category: $2,000 first, $1,000 second, $500 third; distinguished submissions $250. First-place winners enrolling at Bennington receive full tuition for four years; distinguished recipients half tuition for four years; finalists $25,000 per year for four years. Additional scholarship renewal conditions are not published in the contest rules.
deadline: For the 2026-27 awards, September 1, 2026 at 9 a.m. ET through November 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET; winners announced spring 2027.
apply: Submit one typed English entry in one writing category: one fiction story/excerpt, one nonfiction essay/excerpt, or one to three poems, with a strict total limit of 1,500 words including titles, headers, footers and citations. A teacher must review and approve it; homeschooled entrants use a non-parent mentor. Grades 9 to 11 register for the YCA portal; grade 12 completes the free, nonbinding Common or Coalition application and then receives submission instructions.
eligibility: Currently enrolled grades 9 to 12 worldwide, including homeschooled students. Graduates, gap-year and transfer students are excluded. One submission per discipline and one award discipline per student; simultaneous submissions to other competitions/publications are allowed.
notes: Free entry. AI may not be used for brainstorming, creating, drafting, revising or collaboration. Seniors must complete their Bennington application before entering. Student ownership and future publication rights remain, while winning/distinguished work may be showcased. College scholarships require enrollment at Bennington; complete renewal conditions are not published on the award pages.

provider: National Endowment for the Arts / Mid Atlantic Arts / state arts agencies
name: Poetry Out Loud
value: National champion $20,000; second $10,000; third $5,000; fourth through ninth $1,000 each, plus one $1,000 honorable mention from each of three semifinals. State champion $200 and one state runner-up $100. Separate school/organization poetry-material stipends: $500 for national finalists, semifinal honorable mentions and state champions; $200 for state runners-up.
deadline: Local/school entry and competition dates vary by state. State contests must finish by March 7, 2027; state champion and chaperone registration March 10, 2027. National events April 26 to 28, 2027 in Washington, D.C.; final April 28, 2027 at 7 p.m. ET.
apply: Enter through a school or local organization registered with the state coordinator and advance through lower-level contests. Choose only one school/organization competition stream. Prepare three official-anthology poems for state/national finals, including one no more than 25 lines and one published before 1930; one poem can meet both criteria. State winners and chaperones register for the National Finals and submit tax-identification forms for travel.
eligibility: Currently enrolled grades 9 to 12, with an exception for grade 8 students in a grades 9-12 class. Homeschoolers may enter through a willing local school or homeschool competition coordinated with the state. Prior national champions cannot return. Relatives/household members of national organizers cannot advance nationally; relatives of state coordinators and affiliated sponsors/contractors cannot advance beyond school level in that state.
notes: Only versions in the official anthology as of September 1, 2026 are eligible for 2026-27. Each competition needs at least two students. Valid W-9 or W-8BEN forms are required for prizes and arranged travel/lodging; awards are taxable and some foreign recipients face withholding. The national event includes state-champion travel with an adult chaperone. School stipends are separate from student cash awards.

name: National FFA Scholarships
value: Multiple sponsor scholarships through one application; individual amounts, payment periods and renewal requirements vary and the next-cycle award list is not published.
deadline: Next-cycle dates are not published. The official page still lists the 2025-26 application: November 1, 2025 to January 15, 2026; acceptance May 29, 2026.
apply: Use the National FFA scholarship application linked to Kaleidoscope when the next cycle opens. One application considers eligible students for multiple sponsor scholarships; next-cycle application materials are not published.
eligibility: The current directory serves senior FFA members in high school and FFA alumni in college pursuing trade school, vocational certificates, or two- or four-year degrees. Individual sponsor criteria for the next cycle are not published.
notes: This is a collection of sponsor scholarships with different rules. The current page describes nearly $2.5 million across the whole collection, rather than an individual award. It still displays the completed 2025-26 cycle.

provider: American Academy of Neurology / Child Neurology Society
name: AAN Neuroscience Research Prize
value: Three AAN winners receive $1,000 each and a 2027 AAN Annual Meeting poster presentation. Each student and one parent or mentor receive coach airfare, two hotel nights, meeting registration and $100 per day for up to two days. One Bhuwan Garg winner receives $1,000 and a 2027 Child Neurology Society poster presentation, with student/parent-or-mentor airfare, three lodging nights, ground transport and registration. Travel benefits depend on the in-person meeting proceeding.
deadline: Applications opened July 29, 2026; complete application closes October 20, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CT. Notifications by the end of January 2027.
apply: Use the official online application with a maximum 300-word abstract, research report and bibliography. Complete electronic signatures from a parent/guardian, teacher and mentor by the application deadline. First-round judging reviews the abstract; finalists receive full-report review.
eligibility: Students enrolled in and attending grades 9 to 12 in the United States, regardless of age. Individual original neuroscience research and original written work are required; group projects are excluded, but a formal laboratory is not required. Family of judges, AAN Science Committee members or AAN staff are ineligible.
notes: Research must concern the brain or nervous system. Behavioral or psychology projects need a clear neurophysiology connection. Travel packages differ between the three AAN prizes and the Bhuwan Garg prize.

provider: National Center for Women & Information Technology
name: NCWIT Aspirations in Computing High School Award
value: National Winners receive cash and a trip to the Bank of America celebration; the current prize chart does not state the cash amount. National Winners and Honorable Mentions receive an engraved award. Regional Affiliate Winners, Honorable Mentions and Rising Stars receive an engraved medallion. Recognition at a regional event is at the affiliate's discretion.
deadline: Applications September 1, 2026 to October 27, 2026 at 10 p.m. ET. Optional educator endorsement November 5, 2026 at 10 p.m. ET. Under-18 applicants need parent/guardian approval to join the AiC Community before applying.
apply: Join the free AiC Community, then submit the online award application in English or Spanish. It includes four required written responses of 25 to 250 words each, activities, technology access, family education and AI-use disclosure; project/portfolio links are optional. One optional educator endorsement may be requested after submission and is strongly recommended for national consideration.
eligibility: Grades 9 to 12, age 13 or older at account creation, involved in technology and attending a school in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Guam, U.S. Virgin Islands or on a U.S. overseas military base. Under-18 students need guardian approval for Community membership. National designations additionally require U.S. citizenship, permanent residence or the IRS substantial presence test, plus a U.S. tax identification or Social Security number. NCWIT staff, contractors, board members and their specified family/household members are excluded. Prior National Winners cannot win again; regional repeat awards are discretionary.
notes: Canada has a separate award route. There is no gender restriction in the current award eligibility rules. AI tools are allowed with disclosure and authentic personal responses. National Winners must return tax information and a notarized travel waiver and book travel on time or risk forfeiture; award value may be reported on Form 1099.

name: SWE Emerging First Year Scholars
value: Multiple Society-selected scholarships with different sponsor amounts and renewal rules; the 2027-28 individual award list is not published. Current general guidance says funds are paid directly to the student in a single late-fall payment and have no spending restriction.
deadline: The 2027-28 interest form says Emerging First Year applications are expected from early February to the end of March; exact dates will be released in the fall. These are tentative months, not a published deadline.
apply: Sign up on the official 2027-28 interest form for opening notifications; it is not the scholarship application. When open, one application considers all qualifying Society-selected scholarships. Current general guidance requires one recommendation by the application deadline; finalists provide an official transcript and recipients provide a sponsor-facing resume.
eligibility: Students entering their first year of college and enrolling in an ABET-accredited engineering, engineering technology or computer science program. Current general FAQ requires a 3.5 unweighted cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale, with re-entry/nontraditional applicants exempt. Complete sponsor-specific 2027-28 eligibility is not published.
notes: The 2026-27 application is closed; an official 2027-28 interest form is open. This is a collection of merit scholarships; specific donors may consider financial need. SWE's nearly $1.6 million reported for 2025 covers all of its scholarship programs, rather than an individual first-year award. A recommender who has known the applicant at least two years and is not a relative is strongly recommended.

name: Ron Brown Scholarship
value: $40,000 over four years ($10,000 per year), normally 20 scholarships; eligible for an accredited four-year U.S. college in any discipline. Detailed ongoing renewal conditions are not published on the current application page.
deadline: For the 2027 scholarship competition: student application December 1, 2026; school transcript and two recommendations December 15, 2026. Semifinalists interview virtually; finalists attend Washington, D.C. interviews with expenses paid.
apply: Apply online with three essays of approximately 500 words each, academic/activity information and household financial information. After you submit, school officials and recommenders receive requests for the transcript and two letters; at least one letter must be from a counselor, teacher or principal, and the other may not be from a relative. SAT/ACT/AP/IB scores are optional. Semifinalists must verify household income.
eligibility: Black/African American current high school seniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, excel academically, show leadership and service, and demonstrate financial need. Current college students are ineligible. Four-year accredited U.S. undergraduate study is required; vocational or technical training is excluded.
notes: Financial need is required, alongside merit criteria; the FAQ gives no fixed income cutoff. Finalists have virtual alumni conversations and in-person interviews. The official page confirms the 2027 application is open, but complete scholarship renewal criteria are not published.

name: HSF Scholar Program
value: Scholar status provides support services but does not guarantee a cash scholarship. The 2026 program lists $500 to $5,000 cash awards, subject to funds and relative financial need; 2027 amounts and terms are not published.
deadline: 2027 dates are not published. The official timeline is still for 2026: initial deadline February 15, 2026; finalist phase March 2026, selection June 2026 and supporting documents June to November 2026.
apply: Use the online HSF Scholar application when the next cycle opens. The published 2026-27 eligibility page requests that year's FAFSA; its help center lists financial-aid, enrollment, transcript and DACA-specific document questions, but detailed next-cycle instructions are not published.
eligibility: For the published 2026-27 cycle: Hispanic heritage, U.S. citizenship/permanent residence/DACA, at least 3.0/4.0 GPA for high school students or 2.5 for college/graduate students, and full-time enrollment in an accredited public or nonprofit four-year U.S. university or graduate school. Fall 2027 eligibility is not confirmed.
notes: Selection is based on merit; cash depends on available funds and relative need. Scholar recognition and services are separate from a guaranteed monetary award. The current English page still gives 2026-27 study/FAFSA requirements; DACA applicants should check the applicable financial-aid-document instructions when the next cycle opens.

name: JEA Journalist of the Year Scholarship
value: $4,000 for the national winner; $1,200 each for up to five finalists
deadline: State entry deadlines vary and must precede the national round. JEA's 2026-27 calendar confirms national submissions March 15, 2027. The separate award page still shows March 15, 2026 and a general 11:59 p.m. CDT cutoff; 2027 state dates and cutoff details should be confirmed.
apply: Enter the state Journalist of the Year contest first; state winners submit a public online portfolio, transcript or counselor statement, recommendation letters, resume, personal narrative, action/portrait photos and requested contact information through JEA's national application. Follow the state director's submission rules. The award page asks for three letters in its guidelines but says up to three in its FAQ.
eligibility: High school seniors or international equivalent, with a current JEA-member adviser. U.S. entrants must win the state contest. International entrants submit to JEA's global engagement director; judges may advance up to three portfolios, at most one per country. No journalism-major requirement or two-year journalism-experience minimum.
notes: Cash is paid to the winner's college/university account. Current national prizes are $4,000 and up to five $1,200 finalist awards. The national 2027 date is confirmed in JEA's annual calendar, but the award page and state deadline table have not been fully updated for that cycle. Confirm the recommendation count because the guidelines and FAQ differ.

name: Access/VSA Emerging Young Artists Program
value: Current stipend amount, travel coverage and programme obligations could not be confirmed from accessible official rules.
deadline: The 2027 application deadline could not be confirmed from an accessible official source.
apply: The historical official VSA competition used the CaFE artwork portal. The current application link and required portfolio/materials could not be confirmed because the programme page is blocked.
eligibility: Historically this programme served individual visual artists with disabilities, ages 16 to 25, living in the United States, and excluded prior recipients. Current-cycle restrictions could not be confirmed.
notes: The current Kennedy Center programme page is blocked. An older official CaFE call establishes the programme's history, but cannot establish the 2027 theme, stipend, deadline, workshop obligations or current eligibility.

name: International Thespian Society Senior Scholarships
value: Published senior-eligible awards: Dr. Kenny D. Hasija $1,000; Mark Drum $1,250; Alan D. and Penny Lu Engelsman $1,000; Future Theatre Educator $1,500; Board of Directors and Presidents' Leadership $1,000 each; Christopher L. Hunt $1,000; Michael J. Peitz Leadership $1,500. Full payment and renewal terms are not published.
deadline: The Foundation says applications open February 1 to April 1 annually, with May announcements; the Association page says January 1 to April 1. The 2027 cycle year and conflicting opening dates are not resolved.
apply: Inducted Thespians use separate joint applications by award family: Artists of the Future, Theatre Educators of the Future and Leaders of the Future. Linked portals require an EdTA account; public pages do not state the complete application materials for the next cycle.
eligibility: Inducted Thespians who are graduating high school seniors, with award-specific requirements. Engelsman requires theatre or a related major; Future Theatre Educator requires a theatre education major; Hunt requires a business/marketing degree and career; leadership awards require demonstrated leadership. The Mark Drum award also admits undergraduates. Earlier Association descriptions specify racial-background restrictions for Hasija and Drum, while the current Foundation eligibility lines omit them; confirm those award-specific rules in the application.
notes: This is a collection of distinct awards. College-only Gai Laing Jones scholarships, festival attendance aid, chapter awards and Thespy finalist awards have separate eligibility and applications. The current Foundation and Association pages differ on opening month and some background restrictions.

name: JRF Scholarship
value: Up to $35,000 over four years, plus a four-year mentoring/career program and funded attendance at the annual Mentoring and Leadership Conference and other events. Complete academic/payment renewal conditions are not published on the public pages.
deadline: Opens September 1, 2026; application, recommendation and CSS Profile due January 14, 2027 at 5 p.m. EST. Regional virtual semifinalist interviews April to May 2027; decisions June 2027.
apply: Apply online with one adult recommendation, transcript, SAT or ACT score, activities, household details, college plans and three brief essays. Submit the CSS Profile to JRF code 4248 for the main household and any applicable secondary/noncustodial-parent household. All components must arrive by the deadline; no extensions.
eligibility: U.S. citizens graduating high school in spring 2027 and enrolling full time at an accredited JRF-approved four-year U.S. college or U.S.-affiliated university in fall 2027. The FAQ also permits students who graduated the prior year and have taken no college coursework. Applicants need academic excellence, leadership, community service and financial need and must not have accrued more than 25% of graduation credits.
notes: Financial need is required and evaluated individually without a universal published income cutoff. Athletics is not required. Scholars must perform and document community service throughout college. Home-schooled applicants can use a parent-issued transcript. The public pages do not state complete ongoing renewal criteria.

name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
value: Published program: up to $10,000 per year, up to $40,000 total, based on unmet need after the college aid package, plus a paid Amazon internship opportunity. Renew up to three further years or a bachelor's degree, with full-time enrollment, good academic standing and continued eligibility. Upcoming-cycle information is tentative.
deadline: The 2025-26 cycle is closed and next-cycle dates are unpublished. The administrator's old-cycle page gives conflicting January 22 and January 26, 2026 deadlines; neither is a 2027 deadline.
apply: Sign up for opening reminders. Prior published requirements include an online recommendation, transcript, short responses and the first two pages of the most recent household IRS 1040, with sensitive identifiers redacted. Selected recipients provide the college aid award letter. A timed Amazon assessment can substitute for the computer-science course. The next-cycle application is not published.
eligibility: Published/tentative guidance: U.S. high school senior, cumulative GPA at least 2.3/4.0 or equivalent, financial need, and U.S. work authorization valid for at least two years. Complete or take a computer-science course, or take the alternative assessment; pursue an eligible computing-related bachelor's degree through a four-year college or a two-year-to-four-year transfer route. Next-cycle final criteria are unpublished.
notes: The administrator explicitly labels upcoming information tentative. Eligible majors include mathematics/applied mathematics, data science, electrical engineering and other listed computing fields as well as computer science. Awards cover education-related cost-of-attendance expenses after other aid; they are not a guaranteed $40,000. Current renewal guidance describes good standing, typically 2.0 GPA or better, rather than a universal guaranteed threshold.

name: High School Poster Contest
value: First $1,000; second $500; third $250; up to five honorable mentions of $100
deadline: Entries postmarked by February 11, 2027; winners announced May 7, 2027. Digital-entry closing time/time zone is not stated.
apply: Create an original 16-by-20-inch poster, including any border/mat, containing the statement "You can make a difference". Submit a digitally created poster online as a JPG; mail handmade work to The Christophers, 264 W. 40th St., Suite 603, New York, NY 10018. Put student/school/teacher/contact/grade information on the back; protect charcoal, pastels or glitter with laminate or clear plastic and avoid sharp/breakable materials.
eligibility: Students in grades 9 to 12 living in the United States. Each entry must be one student's original concept, design, artwork and photos. AI-created work is ineligible. U.S. citizen/resident winners must supply a Social Security number before a cash prize above $600 is paid.
notes: Free creative contest open to all faiths or none. Digital design tools are allowed, but AI programs are prohibited. All entries become The Christophers' property and are not returned. The current page gives a postmark deadline and permits online digital submissions without a separate online cutoff time.
